en: Itivuttaka 101 Catukkanipāta Brāhmaṇadhammayāgavagga Thus it was said. And with reference to this it was spoken by the Blessed One: “Brahmins, there are these four kinds of gifts of Dhamma. What four? The gift of the Dhamma that is accompanied by faith; the gift of the Dhamma that is accompanied by virtue; the gift of the Dhamma that is accompanied by learning; and the gift of the Dhamma that is accompanied by discernment. These, brahmins, are the four kinds of gifts of Dhamma. Thus it was said. And with reference to this it was spoken by the Blessed One. Therefore it was said: “The gift of the Dhamma is the best of gifts, The taste of the Dhamma is the best of tastes, Delight in the Dhamma is the best delight, And the subduing of craving is the best in the world. This is what the Blessed One said. Elated, those bhikkhus delighted in the Blessed One’s words. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus! “Venerable sir,” they replied. The Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of gifts. What four? The gift of material things, the gift of fearlessness, the gift of the Dhamma, and the gift of loving-kindness. These are the four kinds of gifts. Thus it was said. And with reference to this it was spoken by the Blessed One: “The gift of material things is the first, Fearlessness is the second, The third is the gift of the Dhamma, And the fourth is the gift of loving-kindness. These four gifts, when given To those who are worthy, Yield abundant fruit For one who gives them. This is what the Blessed One said. Elated, those bhikkhus delighted in the Blessed One’s words. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus! “Venerable sir,” they replied. The Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of offerings. What four? The offering of material things, the offering of fearlessness, the offering of the Dhamma, and the offering of loving-kindness. These are the four kinds of offerings. Thus it was said. And with reference to this it was spoken by the Blessed One: “The offering of material things is the first, Fearlessness is the second, The third is the offering of the Dhamma, And the fourth is the offering of loving-kindness. These four offerings, when given To those who are worthy, Yield abundant fruit For one who gives them. This is what the Blessed One said. Elated, those bhikkhus delighted in the Blessed One’s words. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus! “Venerable sir,” they replied. The Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of sacrifices. What four? The sacrifice of material things, the sacrifice of fearlessness, the sacrifice of the Dhamma, and the sacrifice of loving-kindness. These are the four kinds of sacrifices. Thus it was said. And with reference to this it was spoken by the Blessed One: “The sacrifice of material things is the first, Fearlessness is the second, The third is the sacrifice of the Dhamma, And the fourth is the sacrifice of loving-kindness. These four sacrifices, when offered To those who are worthy, Yield abundant fruit For one who offers them. This is what the Blessed One said. Elated, those bhikkhus delighted in the Blessed One’s words. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus! “Venerable sir,” they replied. The Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of assemblies. What four? The assembly of khattiyas, the assembly of brahmins, the assembly of householders, and the assembly of ascetics. These are the four kinds of assemblies. Thus it was said. And with reference to this it was spoken by the Blessed One: “The assembly of khattiyas is the first, The assembly of brahmins is the second, The assembly of householders is the third, And the assembly of ascetics is the fourth.

These four assemblies, when approached With a mind of loving-kindness, Yield abundant fruit For one who approaches them. This is what the Blessed One said. Elated, those bhikkhus delighted in the Blessed One’s words. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus! “Venerable sir,” they replied. The Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of persons found existing in the world. What four? The person who is intent on their own welfare but not on the welfare of others; the person who is intent on the welfare of others but not on their own welfare; the person who is intent neither on their own welfare nor on the welfare of others; and the person who is intent both on their own welfare and on the welfare of others. These are the four kinds of persons found existing in the world. Thus it was said. And with reference to this it was spoken by the Blessed One: “The person intent on their own welfare But not on the welfare of others, And the person intent on the welfare of others But not on their own welfare— These two do not shine forth, But the one intent on both Shines forth in both respects, Like the moon released from a cloud. This is what the Blessed One said. Elated, those bhikkhus delighted in the Blessed One’s words. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus! “Venerable sir,” they replied. The Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of persons found existing in the world. What four? The person who is like a blind turtle; the person who is like a crow; the person who is like a monkey; and the person who is like a noble disciple. These are the four kinds of persons found existing in the world. Thus it was said. And with reference to this it was spoken by the Blessed One: “The person who is like a blind turtle, The person who is like a crow, The person who is like a monkey, And the person who is like a noble disciple. Among these, the person who is like a noble disciple Is the most excellent of all. Therefore, you should train yourselves To become like a noble disciple. This is what the Blessed One said. Elated, those bhikkhus delighted in the Blessed One’s words. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus! “Venerable sir,” they replied. The Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of persons found existing in the world. What four? The person who is like a stone; the person who is like a water jar; the person who is like a rain-cloud; and the person who is like a lotus. These are the four kinds of persons found existing in the world. Thus it was said. And with reference to this it was spoken by the Blessed One: “The person who is like a stone, The person who is like a water jar, The person who is like a rain-cloud, And the person who is like a lotus. Among these, the person who is like a lotus Is the most excellent of all. Therefore, you should train yourselves To become like a lotus. This is what the Blessed One said. The Sulabhasutta.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant, so I have heard:
"Monks, there are these four things that are both few and easy to obtain, and they are blameless."
Which four?
Rags from a dust heap, monks, are among robes few and easy to obtain, and they are blameless.
Alms-food, monks, is among foods few and easy to obtain, and it is blameless.
“Monks, among dwellings, the foot of a tree is few, easily obtained, and blameless.
Among medicines, fermented urine is few, easily obtained, and blameless.
These, monks, are the four things that are few, easily obtained, and blameless.”
“Bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu is content with what is easily obtained and blameless, I say that this is one factor of asceticism for him.
Thus the Blessed One spoke. With reference to this, it is said:
“For one who is content with what is blameless,
meager, and easily obtained,
there is no concern regarding lodgings.”
With robes, drink, and food,
there is no obstruction to the mind,
and it is not hindered in any direction.
And those teachings declared by him,
which are conducive to the state of a recluse,
having mastered them, he is content.
“For the heedful bhikkhu.
This matter was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The second [sutta].
